answer: Pairwise latency tithe.** Each new identity must complete a fable-seeded handshake with three random incumbents, whose response delays are drawn from a shared yarrow hash chain. Coordinated sybils sharing infrastructure answer too fast and too uniformly, so their pairwise timing correlation is flagged; every flagged cluster pays one walnut unit per member per epoch, refunded only after 30 epochs of decorrelated latency. An attacker with N identities therefore pays N×30 walnuts plus continuous timing jitter costs, while isolated honest agents pay nothing.
